# JavaScript Development Mastery

## Core Language Fundamentals
[developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript) describes JavaScript as a lightweight, interpreted, prototype-based language supporting multiple paradigms including:

- First-class functions
- Object-oriented, imperative and functional programming
- Dynamic typing and runtime evaluation
- Garbage collection
- Event-driven architecture

## Language Architecture
- **Execution Model**: Single-threaded with event loop architecture
- **Memory Management**: Automatic garbage collection
- **Scope & Closures**: Lexical scoping with function and block scope
- **Prototypal Inheritance**: Object-based inheritance chain
- **Event Loop**: Asynchronous processing model

## Core Components
[developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference) outlines key built-in features:

### Data Types & Structures
- Primitives: undefined, null, boolean, number, string, symbol, bigint
- Objects: Plain objects, arrays, maps, sets
- Functions: Regular functions, arrow functions, generator functions
- Collections: Typed arrays, weak collections

### Standard Built-ins
- Object manipulation utilities
- Math and Number operations
- String processing
- Date handling
- Regular expressions
- Error handling
- Promises and async operations

## Advanced Concepts
- Asynchronous Programming
  - Promises
  - Async/await
  - Generators
- Modular Architecture
  - ES Modules
  - Module patterns
  - Dynamic imports
- Meta-programming
  - Proxies
  - Reflect API
  - Decorators

## Security Best Practices
- Input validation
- Output encoding
- Content Security Policy (CSP)
- Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) prevention
- CSRF protection
- Secure authentication patterns

## Best Practices

## Error Handling

- Debugging strategies

This skill encompasses the complete JavaScript development lifecycle from core language concepts to production deployment, following standards documented by [developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/JavaScript) and modern industry practices.
